Today we're deciding: Choose a logo direction for the rebrand.
For this simulated decision, I’ll treat the following setup as the shared facts.
Options:
A) Minimalist Geometric Symbol with Bold Colors — production cost: $4,000; adaptability: high across digital platforms; color palette: 4 bold colors (+ Clean, modern look that scales well on all media; − May feel too abstract and lack emotional connection)
B) Vintage Emblem with Hand-Drawn Typography — production cost: $7,500; adaptability: moderate, less flexible on small sizes; color palette: earth tones and muted shades (+ Strong emotional appeal and brand heritage emphasis; − More expensive and less versatile for digital use)
C) Dynamic Abstract Mark with Gradient Effects — production cost: $6,000; adaptability: good for digital but challenging in print; color palette: multi-color gradients (+ Visually striking and trendy, attracts tech-savvy users; − Gradient effects complicate printing and some merchandise)
D) Monogram Lettermark with Serif Font — production cost: $3,500; adaptability: excellent for print and digital; color palette: two-tone classic colors (+ Timeless and professional look with strong brand recognition; − Less visually distinctive and may feel conservative)
Context: The rebrand launch is scheduled in 3 months; Budget for logo finalization and rollout is fixed at $15,000; The decision group has exactly 7 participants with diverse marketing and design backgrounds.
What balance of modern appeal versus brand heritage should our new logo strike?
